is_anopheles.evidence: Page 3: 297 adult female Anopheles mosquitoes (55.5% An. gambiae s.l and 44.5% An. funestus s.s) were collected indoor in Ndjili-Brasserie.

reports_target_markers.evidence: Page 5: Genotyped L1014F-KdrW (Vgsc L995F), L1014S-KdrE (Vgsc L995S), N1575Y-kdr (Vgsc N1570Y), G119S-Ace1 (Ace-1 G280S) in An. gambiae s.l., and A296S-RDL (Rdl A296S), 119F-GSTe2 (GSTe2 L119F), Cyp6P9a_R, Cyp6P9b_R, and 6.5kb-SV in An. funestus s.s.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 5 & Figures 4 and 5 report precise genotype frequencies for F0 females genotyped in 2021 (e.g. An. gambiae L1014F: 98.3% RR, 1.7% SS; L1014S: 89.9% SS, 8.4% RS, 1.7% RR; An. funestus GSTe2 119F: 70.5% RR, 19.6% RS, 9.8% SS; RDL 296S: 2% RR, 26.4% RS, 71.6% SS) with total sample sizes given (N=60 per species group).

african_field_population.evidence: Page 9: Mosquitoes were collected in July 2021 inside households at Ndjili-Brasserie, a suburb of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo.

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical study reporting field collections and laboratory genotyping/bioassays conducted in 2021.

sub_country_location.evidence: Page 9: Ndjili-Brasserie, Kinshasa (4°19′39″S, 15°18′48″E), Democratic Republic of Congo.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Page 9: Adult Anopheles female mosquitoes were collected in July 2021.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study collects new primary data in 2021 and compares it to previously published 2015 baseline data from the same location.

supplement.evidence: All required genotype counts, frequencies, sample sizes, and bioassay data are reported in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide resistance escalation in An. gambiae s.l. and An. funestus s.s. collected in July 2021 in Ndjili-Brasserie, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Target site resistance markers (Vgsc L995F, L995S, N1570Y, Ace-1 G280S, Rdl A296S, GSTe2 L119F, Cyp6p9a_R, Cyp6p9b_R, and Cyp6p9a/b 6.5kb-SV) were genotyped in field-caught F0 females, showing high frequencies of L995F in An. gambiae (98.3% RR) and L119F in An. funestus (70.5% RR).
